learning_outcomes.text: Knows the methods of describing continuous and discrete systems and signals in the time and frequency domains.
Knows the methods for designing analog and discrete filters.
Knows the methods for time and time-frequency analysis of signals.
Knows what adaptive filtering is and how it can be implemented.
Knows how lossy and lossless data compression methods work.
Knows the basic methods of digital image processing.
Can design signal processing and analysis systems.
Can implement signal processing and analysis algorithms.
Can define a complex problem in the field of signal analysis and processing and solve it using available knowledge.
Is able to independently improve knowledge and skills in signal analysis and processing.
Is able to present the results of literature studies (synthesis of knowledge) or their own work in the form of a technical report.

syllabus_topics: Solving a task in the broad field of signal analysis and processing within the project. The project is carried out individually or in groups of two, with a clear distinction of work performed by each person. The project requires: 1. Recognizing the state of knowledge regarding the task (literature review). 2. Depending on the complexity of the task, implementing the whole or a selected fragment of the solution. 3. Testing the implemented solution and evaluating the obtained results.
Generating discrete signals.
Discrete signals - sequences: Deterministic sequences; random sequences; basic operations on sequences.

Discrete systems: Linear system, shift-invariant system; causal system; stability; properties of LTI systems; frequency representation of discrete signals and systems; Fourier representation of sequences.
Discrete convolution and spectrum of a discrete signal.
Analog systems: Laplace transform; transfer function of an analog system; stability.
Designing analog filters.

Z-transform: Transfer function of a discrete system; analysis of LTI system properties; frequency characteristics of a discrete system; all-pass and inverse systems; minimum-phase all-pass decomposition.
Designing recursive IIR digital filters.

Signal sampling: Sampling theorem; reconstruction of a continuous signal from discrete representation; invariant impulse response method; sampling rate conversion; digital signal analysis and processing path.
Designing non-recursive FIR digital filters.
Methods for calculating DFT.
Designing analog filters: Butterworth, Chebyshev, and elliptic filters; frequency transformation - bandpass filters.

Designing digital filters: Bilinear transformation; FIR filters; LTI systems with linear phase characteristic; designing FIR filters using window method; optimal FIR filter - Parks-McClellan algorithm; Hilbert filter and discrete analytical signal; discrete differentiating systems.
Filtering digital signals.
Frequency analysis using DFT.

Discrete Fourier transform: Discrete Fourier Series; discrete Fourier transform; circular convolution; calculating linear convolution using circular convolution; sectioned convolution; Goertzel algorithm; Chirp-Z transform; FFT algorithms; DFT of real-valued signals.
Signal analysis using DFT: DFT analysis of sinusoidal signals; interpolated DFT; short-time Fourier transform, spectrogram; analysis of stationary random signals - periodogram.
Sampling rate conversion. Analytical signal.
Adaptive filters.

Signal approximation, optimal filters and adaptive filters: Signal approximation in multidimensional space; optimal filtering in the least squares sense; RLS adaptive filters; estimation in the minimum mean squares sense; LMS adaptive filters; applications of adaptive filters.
Wavelet transform: Continuous wavelet transform; discrete wavelet transform; predictive DWT.
Wavelet transform.
Entropy coding: Huffman coding; arithmetic coding; dictionary coding.
Signal compression.
Image filtering.
Digital images: 2D filtering; special filters; Fourier transform of images; designing 2D filters using window method; DFT and DWT of images; computed tomography issue.
DFT and DWT of images.
Improving the quality of digital images: Correction of geometric distortions of the camera; blur removal; super-resolution.
Radon transform.
Measurement of sinusoidal signals: PN-EN 61000-4-7 standard; software PLL loop; parametric frequency estimation methods.
assessment_rules: Lectures are verified by an examination. Laboratory and project classes are verified by projects. To pass the module, all laboratory classes must be passed. Student presence at lectures is not explicitly obligatory, but students should ask questions and clarify doubts. Audiovisual recording of lectures requires the lecturer's consent. For laboratory classes, students must prepare for exercises, which may be verified by an oral or written colloquium. The course is passed by presenting a solution to the problem posed in the laboratory classes. For project classes, the method of execution and the final effect of the project are assessed.
